checklists.title: Leaving a building during an alarm
steps: Treat the alarm as real until it is officially confirmed otherwise.
Stop non-essential tasks and take only what you can carry in a few seconds.
Use the stairs, not the elevator.
Feel a closed door with the back of your hand. If it is hot, do not open it and use another route.
In smoke, stay low, cover your nose and mouth, keep one hand on the wall and close doors behind you.
Go to the assembly point, report to the person doing the headcount, and do not go back in until responders say it is safe.

checklists.title: Severe bleeding
steps: Check that the scene is safe first, so you do not become a second casualty.
Call 112 or the local emergency number. Give the location, what happened, the number of injured people and any hazards.
Press firmly and directly on the wound with a clean cloth or dressing, and keep the pressure on.
If the cloth soaks through, add more layers on top instead of removing it.
Keep the person lying down and warm, and monitor them until help arrives.
Hand over to responders: what happened, what you found, what you did and when, and any changes since.

checklists.title: Burns
steps: Deal with life-threatening problems first: not breathing and severe bleeding.
Cool the burn under cool running water for 10 to 20 minutes.
Do not apply ice, butter, oils or toothpaste, and do not burst blisters.
Cover the burn loosely with a clean, non-fluffy dressing.
Seek medical help for large or deep burns, burns on the face, hands or genitals, or if you are unsure.
